headline_marked: [[AI Code Analysis]] goes from 'You Have a Bug' to 'Here's the Root Cause'
headline: AI Code Analysis goes from 'You Have a Bug' to 'Here's the Root Cause'
summary: A developer built an app review pipeline that now uses AI to pinpoint specific files and lines causing bugs, offering actionable fixes.
details: A developer's app review pipeline, initially classifying issues, was enhanced to automatically identify the root cause of bugs and suggest fixes.
The enhanced pipeline uses a PydanticAI agent with read-only tools to explore the codebase, aiming to reduce manual debugging time from hours to minutes.
Key to the system's efficiency is a generated repo map, providing the AI agent with a 'GPS' of the codebase to speed up investigation and avoid excessive API calls.
To further optimize analysis, a funnel progressively restricts the agent's tools, reducing average tool calls from over 40 to 8-12 without sacrificing quality.
The architecture is designed to be pluggable, allowing integration with various LLM backends such as Grok Build, Claude Code, or OpenAI Codex for deeper analysis.
caption:
Tired of just knowing 'you have a bug'? This developer built an AI pipeline that finds the exact line of code causing it.

A developer's app review pipeline, initially classifying issues, was enhanced to automatically identify the root cause of bugs and suggest fixes.

The enhanced pipeline uses a PydanticAI agent with read-only tools to explore the codebase, aiming to reduce manual debugging time from hours to minutes.

Key to the system's efficiency is a generated repo map, providing the AI agent with a 'GPS' of the codebase to speed up investigation and avoid excessive API calls.

To further optimize analysis, a funnel progressively restricts the agent's tools, reducing average tool calls from over 40 to 8-12 without sacrificing quality.

The architecture is designed to be pluggable, allowing integration with various LLM backends such as Grok Build, Claude Code, or OpenAI Codex for deeper analysis.

headline_marked: [[Kimi Work]] launches beta for AI agents on Mac
headline: Kimi Work launches beta for AI agents on Mac
summary: New platform allows users to run frontier open models locally on their Mac, with support for models from Google, Cohere, and Liquid AI.
details: Kimi Work has launched a beta version of its platform, enabling users to run advanced open AI models directly on their Mac devices.
The platform supports a range of frontier models, including those developed by Google, Cohere, and Liquid AI, offering users flexibility in choosing the best model for their needs.
Nativ, the system behind Kimi Work, is designed to recommend the optimal partner model based on your specific hardware capabilities, ensuring smooth performance.
This development allows for local execution of AI models, potentially enhancing privacy and reducing reliance on cloud-based services.
caption:
Run Google, Cohere, and Liquid AI models locally on your Mac with Kimi Work.

Kimi Work has launched a beta version of its platform, enabling users to run advanced open AI models directly on their Mac devices.

The platform supports a range of frontier models, including those developed by Google, Cohere, and Liquid AI, offering users flexibility in choosing the best model for their needs.

Nativ, the system behind Kimi Work, is designed to recommend the optimal partner model based on your specific hardware capabilities, ensuring smooth performance.

This development allows for local execution of AI models, potentially enhancing privacy and reducing reliance on cloud-based services.
